findings.title: Insert-time eviction silently discards spans and can produce incomplete segments
findings.body: When a segment exceeds 1000 members, `zpopmin` silently removes the lowest-scored (earliest `end_timestamp_precise`) spans without any metric, log, or marker that the segment was truncated. The remaining segment is later flushed as if complete. This replaces the previous `_load_segment_data` behaviour of detecting oversized segments and logging/metric-ing `segment_span_count_exceeded`, and changes the cap from `max_segment_spans=1001` in Python to a hardcoded 1000 in Lua, so legitimate large segments lose spans invisibly.

findings.title: Redirect chain traversal limit reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The loop that follows `span-buf:sr:` redirects now stops after 1000 hops instead of 10000, and the comment explaining that deeper segment trees may not be joined correctly was removed. Segment trees deeper than 1000 will now be split into multiple segments (wrong `set_key`, wrong segment/root attribution) where they previously assembled correctly, with no test covering deep chains near the new limit.

findings.title: SET-to-ZSET conversion breaks on existing Redis data during deployment
findings.body: `process_spans` now `zadd`s to `span-buf:s:*` keys and the Lua script uses `zcard`/`zunionstore`, while `_load_segment_data` uses `zscan`. Any segment keys already stored as plain SETs by the previous version (written with `sadd`) will raise Redis WRONGTYPE errors when touched by the new code, so in-flight segments at deploy time will error out / be lost instead of being flushed. No migration, dual-read, or versioned key prefix is provided.

findings.title: Flush-side max_segment_spans guard removed with no replacement for pre-existing/oversized keys
findings.body: The check that skipped and logged segments with more than `max_segment_spans` spans was deleted from `_load_segment_data`. The only remaining cap is the new Lua insert-time cap of 1000, which does not apply to keys created before this change, keys written by still-running old consumers during a rolling deploy, or the `max_segment_bytes`-only path; such segments are now loaded and flushed regardless of span count, and `self.max_segment_spans` is left as dead configuration.

findings.title: Required end_timestamp_precise lookup can crash the consumer on spans lacking the field
findings.body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises `KeyError` for any ingest-spans message without that field (the existing consumer test payload did not include it until this PR added it). A single such message fails `process_batch` and, being redelivered, can poison-pill the batch instead of being handled or defaulted. The new `Span.end_timestamp_precise` field in buffer.py is likewise a required positional field, breaking any other `Span(...)` constructors that were not updated.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle the datetime ordering it is wired into
findings.body: `get_item_key` does `math.floor(value)`/`math.ceil(value)` on the raw attribute, copying `Paginator` instead of `DateTimePaginator`. `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` passes `order_by="-datetime"`, so `value` is a `datetime` and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError` on the first result whenever `optimized_pagination=true` is used by a superuser/global-access member. The optimized audit-log path therefore 500s rather than paginating.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets reach queryset slicing despite Django forbidding negative indexing
findings.body: Cursor values are client-supplied (`Cursor.from_string` accepts a negative offset), and with `enable_advanced_features=True` the code passes `cursor.offset` straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, claiming in comments that 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' and that this is safe. Django querysets explicitly raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so a crafted `cursor=...:-5:...` request crashes the endpoint (500/DoS); if the queryset were ever a plain sequence the same code would instead wrap around and return rows from the end of the result set, bypassing the intended page window. The same unguarded negative-offset path was left in `BasePaginator.get_result` (line 182) for `is_prev` cursors, affecting all existing paginators.

findings.title: Unrelated, undocumented optimized_pagination switch changes audit-log API behaviour
findings.body: This PR is described as a spans-buffer optimization, but it adds a new `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter and a superuser/`has_global_access` gate that swaps the audit-log endpoint to a different paginator class. That is an unreviewed API contract/behaviour change bundled into the spans change: cursor format and results now depend on the caller's privileges, and (per the paginator defects) the privileged path is broken, with no endpoint tests covering either branch.

findings.title: No test exercises eviction, the 1000-span cap, or deep redirect chains
findings.body: The test changes only add the now-required `end_timestamp_precise` argument to existing Span constructions (all with the identical timestamp 1700000000.0). Nothing inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment to verify which spans `zpopmin` evicts (including whether the root/segment span can be evicted, invalidating `has_root_span` flushing), nothing verifies ordering by differing `end_timestamp_precise` scores after `zunionstore` merges, and nothing covers redirect chains over 1000 hops. The core new behaviour of the PR is therefore untested, as is the new OptimizedCursorPaginator/audit-log path.
